authoring.question: q-125457
authoring.value: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{1}{y}\,i-\frac{1}{x}\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ Interpret circulation as the sum of four convergent improper line integrals over the open quadrant arcs, with independent one-sided limits at $(\pm1,0)$ and $(0,\pm1)$. The field is undefined at those four points, so the original ordinary circulation is not defined.
authoring.rationale: Supply the omitted convergent improper-integral convention. Four independently convergent quadrant integrals yield -4pi; ordinary original circulation remains undefined.

decisions.reason: Retain the verified mathematical correction instead of reimporting the source error

authoring.question: q-125457
authoring.value:
The original field is undefined at the four axis intersections, so an ordinary line integral over the whole circle is not defined. For the explicit improper interpretation, $r(t)=(\cos t,\sin t)$ traverses the unit circle counterclockwise. On each open quadrant arc,

$$\frac{1}{y}\,dx=\frac{-\sin t}{\sin t}\,dt=-dt,\qquad-\frac{1}{x}\,dy=\frac{-\cos t}{\cos t}\,dt=-dt.$$

Thus the scalar pullback is $-2$. Each endpoint has the finite one-sided limit $-2$, so each open-arc integral converges absolutely and equals $-\pi$. Their sum is $\Gamma_{\mathrm{imp}}=-4\pi$, the unchanged option a. No principal-value cancellation is used, and $F$ remains undefined at the excluded points.
authoring.rationale: Supply the omitted convergent improper-integral convention. Four independently convergent quadrant integrals yield -4pi; ordinary original circulation remains undefined.
